# Original registration UTF-7 checker corpus

`original.json` records the unchanged checker's107 generated byte inputs and
CPython3.12.15 UTF-7 `errors=replace` results. The corpus-generating statements
were extracted unchanged from the original AST; expectations never come from
the Rust decoder under test. The checker source SHA and complete fixture hash
are validated. This fixed corpus retires the comparison command, not a generic
CPython codec or unrelated registration tooling.

Twenty-two original checker executions record runner argv, success/failure,
report contents and stdout under controlled child responses. Cases cover
malformed/padded/truncated/direct-byte/surrogate decoding, bool/float Python
JSON equality, changed values, cardinality, Unicode line separators, invalid
JSON/UTF8, nonzero child exits and missing/report-directory output paths.

Independent real CLI probes add the Python report serializer boundary:
992 nested candidate arrays write a mismatch report;993 or more raise before
creating it. The native test preserves the same report/no-report behavior.
`actual-cli-provenance.json` records the independent final eight CLI probes:
depths992/993/994/1000 with empty and scalar leaves, unchanged original source
identity, native binary identity and report creation outcomes. These probes use
the original CLI context, not a runpy frame with a different recursion boundary.
Original scripts/logs remain in private scratch2026-10-18-utf7-check and
2026-10-18-utf7-independent-review. These are host tool/decoder comparisons,
not device, network registration or driving acceptance.
